questions.question: You’re at a party and someone spills their drink on your new shirt. What would be the most appropriate way to respond?
options: Don’t worry about it, it’s not my fault!
Oh no, I’m so sorry! Here, let me help you clean it up.
That’s fine, it’s not my problem.
You shouldn’t have done that—it’s your own mistake.
questions.answer: Oh no, I’m so sorry! Here, let me help you clean it up.

questions.question: Your colleague says, ‘We should move the meeting to 3 PM to avoid traffic.’ How would you respond if you disagree?
options: That’s a great idea! Let’s do it.
I think it’s better to keep it at 2 PM—it’s less chaotic.
We’ll definitely need to move it to 3 PM, then.
Traffic is always better at 3 PM, so let’s go with that.
questions.answer: I think it’s better to keep it at 2 PM—it’s less chaotic.

questions.question: A friend asks, ‘Would you like to come to my birthday party this weekend?’ How would you politely decline?
options: Yes, that sounds amazing! I’ll be there.
I’m afraid I can’t make it—I’ve got plans.
No, I don’t like parties.
Maybe next time, then.
questions.answer: I’m afraid I can’t make it—I’ve got plans.

questions.question: Your boss says, ‘Can you take over the project next week?’ What is the most appropriate way to offer help?
options: No, I can’t take it—I’m too busy.
Of course, I’d be happy to help with that.
That’s a good idea, but I’m not sure I can.
You shouldn’t ask me that—it’s too much work.
questions.answer: Of course, I’d be happy to help with that.

questions.question: At a formal dinner, someone asks, ‘Would you like to join us for dessert?’ What would be the most appropriate response?
options: No, thank you—I’m full.
I’d love to, but I’m not allowed to eat sweets.
That would be lovely, but I’m afraid I can’t.
Yes, I’ll have whatever you’re having.
questions.answer: That would be lovely, but I’m afraid I can’t.
